newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU warns on Caribbean banana trade benefits.
newsitem.headline: EU warns on Caribbean banana trade benefits.

text.p: Caribbean banana exporting countries face economic disaster if a United States complaint against trade preferences granted by the European Union is successful, the European Commission said on Tuesday.

The warning came as the World Trade Organisation prepared on Tuesday to deliver an initial ruling on the U.S. claim that the benefits granted under the Lome Convention discriminate against bananas from U.S.-owned plantations in Latin America.
"Since October 1994 the US authorities have pursued a strategy which if successful would lead directly to the destruction of the Caribbean banana industry," the Commission said in a memorandum.
"It would provoke severe economic hardship and political instability in a region already struggling against considerable difficulty and deprivation," it added.

Caribbean producers - Belize, Surinam, Jamaica and the Windward Islands - account for only three percent of World banana exports and represent only seven percent of the EU market, their only outlet, according to the Caribbean Banana Exporters' Association.

Almost two-thirds of EU banana imports are supplied by Latin America. In 1995, the EU imported 2.65 million tonnes of bananas under a reduced tariff quota, almost exclusively from Latin America. Duty free imports from Caribbean and African exporters totalled just under 680,000 tonnes.
The U.S. produces only 5,000 tonnes of bananas annually and all the home-grown bananas are produced and consumed in Hawaii.
The Commission said that the WTO case was triggered by a complaint from Chiquita Brands International Inc and the Hawaii Banana Industry Association.
The U.S. has also claimed that since 1993, EU banana import rules have hurt Latin American exporters with shipments from Ecuador, Honduras, Guatemala and Mexico falling by 27 percent.
